analysis:
The sole production change in ProviderLoop+Serve.swift:108 assigns the verified-weight-hash persistence path when host services are enabled, before startup preload (126) and coordinator registration (174–193). Surrounding source preserves process-key registration/resumption (180, 205–212), connection-authorization invalidation (415–426), authenticated cache-scope forwarding (324–338), cancellation, and teardown. Registration attestation still signs captured binary/runtime claims with a fresh build invocation (580–601). No supplied change weakens these controls or introduces prompt/key logging, billing changes, or privileged fan access.
ProviderLoop+Testing.swift adds internal setters for the persistence URL and weight-hasher closure (patch head:144–151); these follow existing internal test seams and show no remote or public entry point. Metadata shows no rename or mode change. No concrete regression is established in these units.
Integration must examine VerifiedWeightHashStore.path(), its read/write implementation, and loadWeightHasher/captureWeightHash consumers elsewhere in the PR. In particular, determine whether operator-writable persisted hashes become trusted without fresh cryptographic verification, whether snapshots remain bound to the bytes actually loaded, and whether persistence failure affects availability. These contracts matter to A-004, T-012/T-027 and T-041's verified weightHash SSD binding, but their implementation is outside this supplied source scope. Also reconcile local endpoint startup at Serve.swift:99–101 preceding path assignment at 108 with any concurrent load/persistence logic. This is an unresolved integration question, not evidence of a vulnerability. Only selected threat definitions were supplied in full; this review does not revalidate unchanged dependencies.
